name: Strong Password
description: Monocarp finally got the courage to register on ForceCoders. He came up with a handle but is still thinking about the password. He wants his password to be as strong as possible, so he came up with the following criteria: the length of the password should be exactly $$$m$$$; the password should only consist of digits from $$$0$$$ to $$$9$$$; the password should not appear in the password database (given as a string $$$s$$$) as a subsequence (not necessarily contiguous). Monocarp also came up with two strings of length $$$m$$$: $$$l$$$ and $$$r$$$, both consisting only of digits from $$$0$$$ to $$$9$$$. He wants the $$$i$$$-th digit of his password to be between $$$l_i$$$ and $$$r_i$$$, inclusive. Does there exist a password that fits all criteria?
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of testcases. The first line of each testcase contains a string $$$s$$$ ($$$1 \le |s| \le 3 \cdot 10^5$$$), consisting only of digits from $$$0$$$ to $$$9$$$ — the password database. The second line contains a single integer $$$m$$$ ($$$1 \le m \le 10$$$) — the required length of the password. The third line contains a string $$$l$$$ ($$$|l| = m$$$), consisting only of digits from $$$0$$$ to $$$9$$$ — the lower restriction on each digit. The fourth line contains a string $$$r$$$ ($$$|r| = m$$$), consisting only of digits from $$$0$$$ to $$$9$$$ — the upper restriction on each digit. $$$l_i \le r_i$$$ for all $$$i$$$ from $$$1$$$ to $$$m$$$. The sum of lengths of $$$s$$$ over all testcases doesn't exceed $$$3 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each testcase, print " YES " if there exists a password that fits all criteria. Print " NO " otherwise.
approach_summary: Express count as f(R) - f(L-1). Define memoized state dp[pos][tight][leading_zeros][cond] scanning digits from most to least significant in O(digits × base × states).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1845C — Strong Password [439. Digit DP]
topic_editorial.summary: Digit DP counting values in range $[L, R]$.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Counting valid integers in range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into $f(R) - f(L-1)$, where $f(X)$ counts valid integers in $[0, X]$. Numbers $\le X$ can be formed digit-by-digit from the most significant position. The constraint that the prefix does not exceed $X$ is tracked by a single boolean flag `tight`.
